stimulus.text:
“And I do hereby further declare all indented Servants, Negroes, or others, (appertaining to Rebels,) free that are able and willing to bear Arms, they joining His MAJESTY'S Troops as soon as may be, for the more speedily reducing this Colony to a proper Sense of their Duty, to His MAJESTY'S Crown and Dignity.”
—Lord Dunmore, royal governor of Virginia, Proclamation, November 7, 1775 (abridged)
stimulus.source_note: Lord Dunmore's Proclamation, November 7, 1775. Public domain.

source: original; stimulus viewed before writing — Lord Dunmore's Proclamation, November 7, 1775, public domain.

books.section: Topic 3.5 The American Revolution, A. The War for Independence

stem: According to the proclamation, Dunmore offered freedom to enslaved people who

options.text: Had already escaped to the North before the war
options.misconception: The offer is to those who will join the king's troops now, not to people who already escaped to the North.

options.text: Were owned by Loyalists loyal to the king
options.misconception: The offer covers only enslaved people belonging to rebels; those owned by Loyalists are not included.

options.text: Agreed to work on British ships without pay
options.misconception: The proclamation offers freedom for bearing arms in the king's troops, not for unpaid work on ships.

options.text: Belonged to rebels and could bear arms for Britain

rationales.D: The offer is narrow: it covers servants and enslaved people appertaining to rebels, who are able and willing to bear arms for the king.
rationales.A: The offer looks forward, to those who will join the troops, not backward to people who already escaped.
rationales.B: Loyalists' enslaved people are excluded; the offer is aimed at the property of rebels.
rationales.C: The condition is bearing arms in the king's troops, not working on ships without pay.
rationales.general:
1. Read the condition. Freedom goes to those able and willing to bear arms, joining the king's troops.
2. Read the limit. Only those appertaining to rebels — belonging to Patriots — are covered.
3. Name the offer. Freedom in exchange for military service, aimed at the rebels' labor force, not a general emancipation.
Remember: an offer's limits are its meaning — read who is included and who is left out.
